chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The time of al-Fajr (dawn prayer) is when the dawn breaks until the morning brightens the sky, and it is not befitting to delay that deliberately; but it is a time (of leeway) for the one who is occupied, or forgets, or sleeps.

key_terms.رُخْصَة: Leeway/accommodation — the extended window granted to the excused
key_terms.عَمْدًا: Deliberately/intentionally — the key qualifier that makes delay sinful
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْفَجْرِ: The prescribed time window for the Fajr prayer
key_terms.يَتَجَلَّلَ الصُّبْحُ السَّمَاءَ: The morning brightens the sky — the end of the Fajr prayer window
key_terms.يَنْشَقُّ الْفَجْرُ: True dawn breaks — refers to al-fajr al-sadiq (the true dawn), distinguished from the false dawn (al-fajr al-kadhib)

ai.seo_question: What is the time for Fajr prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the prescribed time window for the Fajr prayer: it begins at true dawn (subh al-sadiq, when the first light appears on the horizon) and extends until the morning light fills the sky. Deliberate delay beyond this window is forbidden, but those who miss it due to preoccupation, forgetfulness, or sleep retain a valid excuse and must pray when able. This ruling reflects the jurisprudential principle that hardship warrants accommodation (rukhsa), demonstrating the balance between strict obligation and pastoral mercy in Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The time for Al-Fajr is when the dawn breaks up to when the morning brightens the sky, and it is not befitting for you to delay that deliberately, but it is a time (leeway) for the one who is busy, or forgets, or sleeps’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali has narrated from his father ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The time for morning Salah (prayer) begins when dawn opens, until morning (with rays) brightens the sky. It is not proper to delay purposely; however, there is time for those who are preoccupied, forget or are sleeping.”
